faq.q: Does adding text actually hide the original content underneath?
faq.a: No. Added text sits as a new layer on top of the PDF; the original text underneath still exists in the file and remains selectable. To truly cover something, use the Whiteout/Redact tool to draw an opaque box over it first, then write on top. The tool shows this warning in the editor precisely because people assume covering text removes it.

faq.q: What can I add besides text?
faq.a: Six tools: Add Text (12 standard fonts in regular/bold/italic variants, size 6–120, colour, opacity and −180 to 180 rotation), Stamp Image/Signature (PNG or JPEG, capped to 400/800/1400px by a quality setting), Rectangle (outlined or filled), Line, Whiteout/Redact, and Highlight in yellow, green, blue or pink. You click or drag on the page to place each; items can be dragged, scaled and deleted.

faq.q: Can it handle rupee signs, Hindi or other non-Latin text?
faq.a: Yes. The standard PDF fonts only cover basic Latin, so if your text contains a rupee sign, Devanagari, emoji or similar, the tool lazily downloads a Noto Sans Devanagari Unicode font (about 640KB on first save) and embeds a subset. Common Word smart-quotes and dashes are folded to plain equivalents. If the font can't load, unsupported characters are stripped so the rest still saves.

Download the edited PDF directly, or Export ZIP to get the PDF plus one composited PNG per page at 72, 144 or 216 DPI. There's also a "Copy annotation list" button that copies every annotation grouped by page. Undo/redo keeps up to 50 steps, and your chosen annotation style (fonts, colours, sizes) is remembered in local storage between visits. Everything runs in your browser.
